Samira — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front, and I can follow with a compact spreadsheet and a recommended credit sheet if that helps:

- Batching: for 18-token requests our continuous batching windows will still give 20–35% token-cost reduction in steady state vs single-shot in hosted environment, depending on concurrency. The biggest lever is prefix/KV cache hit rate — if you have frequent repeated prompts or session continuation, we often see another ~25% on top of batching.

- Quantization: 4-bit on LlamaX tends to cut inference CPU/GPU cost per token by ~35–45% depending on kernel efficiency. For prompt/short-chat heavy workloads the quality delta is typically small but measurable on a few failure modes (numeric precision in tabular data, subtle instruction-following). We recommend a small eval set (10–20k examples) to validate.

- Commercial pilot: a 3-month bucket sized to cover expected peak QPS for a 2–3 week ramp is common — many customers take a 30–40% credit on projected first-quarter spend and then negotiate conversion bands. I can propose a conservative and an aggressive credit tier as two options.

I'll pull a quick usage snapshot template and an initial pricing sheet. Looping in Dylan and Karthik to confirm technical assumptions and provide quant/profile guidance.

Thanks,

Quick, practical responses (keeping it short for procurement):

1) Batching + KV cache impact
- For requests with avg length 18 tokens: expect ~25% token-level batching savings at 50–200 TPS with our default batching window in hosted mode; savings improve with higher concurrency.
- KV cache: if sessions are sticky and requests reuse recent context (same user thread), expect an additional 20–30% savings on token compute after warmup. If traffic is mostly one-off queries, cache helps less.
- Operational note: set autoscale policy to prefer lower latency SLO for open-market hours and increase max-inflight to allow more batching during peaks.

2) Quantization (LlamaX)
- Recommendation: start with a 4-bit asymmetric quant profile we call q4a-fast (balanced speed/quality). For numerical-heavy prompts enable a fallback path to q8 for any numeric-extraction prompts (cheap to detect).
- Expected perf delta: 40% lower token compute cost vs fp16; throughput increases 1.6–2x depending on GPU kernels.
- Risk: edge-case hallucinations in tables/financial-precision tasks — plan: run a 12k prompt eval with priority checks (acct numbers, currency conversions).
- Rollback: can autoswitch to fp16 or q8 at route-level in ~30s for live traffic.

3) Pilot credit structures (two options)
A) Conservative
- 3-month pilot bucket = estimated first-month spend * 1.5.
- Quant: q4a-fast enabled by default; fallback to q8 allowed but charged at fp16-equivalent rate.
- Conversion incentive: 12% one-time reduction on committed annual if they sign within 45 days of pilot end.

B) Aggressive (conversion-focused)
- 3-month pilot bucket = estimated first-month spend * 2.5 (larger cushion).
- Deeper commitment bands: 20% annual discount for a 12-month commit with usage floors.
- Additional: $25k implementation credit to cover eval work + joint case study rights.

Attachments to include: a simple pilot_pricing_sheet and a quant_profile_recs doc. I can also generate a small eval CLI script to run against their sample prompts.

—Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samira — thanks for the patience while we pulled numbers together. Below is a concise proposal that Procurement can drop into their packet; I attached the pilot_pricing_sheet.pdf and quant_profile_recs.md for detail.

Executive summary
- For FastFin's short-chat workload we estimate total token-cost savings of 45–60% when combining batching + KV cache warmup + 4-bit quant (q4a-fast), versus a baseline fp16 single-shot config. Expected variance +/- 8% depending on cache hit rates.

Pilot offer (3 months) — two options for Procurement
1) Conservative option (low friction)
- Pilot bucket: projected month-1 spend * 1.5 (covers nominal ramp + 20% buffer).
- Default runtime: q4a-fast; fallback to q8 for numeric-heavy routes.
- Conversion incentive: 12% recurring discount on a 12-month commitment signed within 45 days of pilot close.

2) Conversion-accelerator option (preferred if FastFin wants stronger move-to-prod cadence)
- Pilot bucket: projected month-1 spend * 2.5.
- Additional $25k implementation credit toward onboarding and evaluation tooling if FastFin commits to a 12-month agreement within the pilot window.
- Deeper discount bands: up to 20% on recurring usage depending on committed volume.

Technical guardrails and asks (for your engineering packet)
- Provide a 10–15k prompt evaluation set representative of your short-chat queries (we can host a secure upload).
- Route-level instrumentation: add a small flag to route numeric-extraction prompts so we can automatically route to q8 for those calls. Simple heuristic is a regex on currency/IBAN patterns.
- Autoscaling: set a higher max-inflight during market open windows to improve batching efficiency; we can share recommended values after viewing your baseline TPS.

Attachments
- pilot_pricing_sheet.pdf (three-line commercial summary + conversion table)
- quant_profile_recs.md (recommended presets, rollback steps, CLI eval script)
- fastfin_usage_snapshot.csv (sample we requested; you can replace with your real CSV)

Next steps
- If Procurement is comfortable, choose Option 1 or Option 2 and we will:
  a) Draft a short pilot SOW (2–3 pages) and an addendum for the conversion discounts.
  b) Dylan will run the quant eval on your sample prompts and share a short quality dashboard within 5 business days.
  c) Engineering kickoff for instrumentation and routing.

Would you like me to propose language for the SOW and conversion addendum directly in this thread? Happy to draft.

Best,
